aboutSection.firstText: Resiliency Gardens plants the seeds of resilience by investing in school gardens, intergenerational learning, and locally driven partnerships that help children and youth actively participate in sustainable food systems, strengthen their own well-being, and care for the health of our planet.
aboutSection.secondText: The deterioration of our natural environment endangers our well-being and future of today’s youth. By equipping youth with critical thinking, problem-solving skills, and resilience, we prepare them to tackle global challenges and become responsible citizens committed to a sustainable future.

mattersSection.title: Why it matters
mattersSection.firstText: The deterioration of our natural environment endangers our well-being and future of today’s youth.
mattersSection.secondText: By equipping youth with critical thinking, problem-solving skills, and resilience, we prepare them to tackle global challenges and become responsible citizens committed to a sustainable future.

solutionSection.title: Our Work
solutionSection.description: Resiliency Gardens began in 2022 as a compassionate response to the urgent need to support Ukrainian refugee children integrating into Polish schools. What began as a group of individual school garden grants has grown into citywide partnerships, local educator networks, and new models for environmental and sustainable food-system learning.

schoolGardens.title: School Gardens: Where the Work Takes Root
schoolGardens.firstText: Resiliency Gardens partners with schools to create outdoor classrooms and living laboratories where students connect with food, nature, the environment and each other.
schoolGardens.secondText: Through hands-on planting, tending, and harvesting, young people discover how healthy ecosystems and communities are grown and leave with a deeper sense of their own role in shaping a more resilient, sustainable world.

educationalPartners.title: Educational Partners: The local leaders who bring educational gardening to life
educationalPartners.firstText: Resiliency Gardens works through locally led educational partners who know their communities, schools, teachers, and children.
educationalPartners.secondText: They transform garden infrastructure into meaningful learning experiences by working directly with teachers, children, youth, families, seniors, and community volunteers.

modelCities.title: Model Cities: Helping Cities Grow Public School Garden Programs
modelCities.text: Resiliency Gardens helps cities bring schools, local educators, businesses, civic leaders, and community volunteers together around a shared goal: making garden-based environmental education accessible to more children. Our model city approach supports public school garden programs that can be adapted and replicated by other communities.

first.title: Start a school or community garden
first.text: Starting a school or community garden is a powerful way to bring people together, foster hands-on learning, and promote healthy living. These gardens serve as living classrooms that teach sustainable practices, connect individuals with nature, and inspire a sense of pride in growing and sharing fresh, nutritious food.

firstItem.title: Grant Opportunities
firstItem.text: As funds become available, ResiliencyGardens.org provides support for school and community garden infrastructure, covering expenses for construction materials, soil, seeds, and tools, as well as educational resources, including instructors and workshops. We invite you to explore our grant programs below to find the one that best suits your needs.

secondItem.title: Inclusive Educational Gardens in Polish Schools

second.title: Start your own garden
second.subtext: Anyone can grow vegetables and everyone enjoys watching a seed they planted sprout and grow. Whether on a windowsill, a balcony or in a garden bed, we can all make a difference.
second.firstText: People who have access to their own vegetable garden consume 40% more fresh vegetables and herbs and, consequently, eat less junk food.
second.secondText: Vegetables and herbs lose 30-50% of their useful properties within 5-10 days. Local vegetable gardens allow you to eat vegetables and herbs immediately after harvesting.
second.thirdText: Working in a garden has a positive effect on personal well-being and gardening with others enhances social connections.

startSection.title: Where to start?
startSection.firstText: If you’ve no land, it doesn’t mean you can’t garden.
startSection.secondText: A garden has four basic needs:

pointsSection.title: Soil.
pointsSection.text: Great soil is essential to growing vegetables, fruits, and other plant life.

pointsSection.title: Sun.
pointsSection.text: Most vegetables need at least 6 hours of unobstructed sun or artificial light per day, although some crops, such as broccoli, lettuce, spinach, and other greens, can tolerate less.

pointsSection.title: Water.
pointsSection.text: Plants need water for essential biological processes that enable them to grow, thrive and reproduce.

pointsSection.title: Seeds.
pointsSection.text: Source and buy quality seeds locally that are suitable for your climate and your type of garden.

tripsBeyondClassroom.name: Trips Beyond the Classroom
tripsBeyondClassroom.description: Helped launch Resiliency Gardens' first pilot Warsaw region during the 2022/23 academic year. By using nature as a shared language, Trips Beyond the Classroom helped children build practical gardening skills, resilience, teamwork, and community.

fundacjaRozwoju.name: Fundacja Naturalnego Rozwoju
fundacjaRozwoju.description: Is the local educational partner supporting the Rybnik Model City school garden program through hands-on environmental education workshops, teacher support, and school-based learning activities focused on nature, food, and sustainability.

ogrodZKlasa.name: Ogród z Klasą / Classy Garden
ogrodZKlasa.description: Is the Kraków-based educational partner helping design the Resiliency Gardens Incubator, including a School Garden Starter Kit and teacher workshop model to help more schools launch practical garden-based learning.

ogrodPodGwiazdami.name: Ogród Pod Gwiazdami / Under the Stars Garden
ogrodPodGwiazdami.description: Is a community garden partner in Kraków providing the demonstration site for the Resiliency Gardens Incubator, including a dedicated children's educational garden where the starter-kit model is being tested and refined.

educators.title: Individual Garden Educators
educators.intro: In addition to our organizational partners, Resiliency Gardens works with individual garden educators who bring hands-on environmental education directly to schools. These educators design and lead workshops that help children learn by planting, observing, building, tasting, and caring for living gardens.

bozena.name: Bożena Mrozek
bozena.school: Przedszkole nr 3, Rybnik and Zespół Szkolno-Rewalidacyjny "Szkoła Życia," Rybnik
bozena.description: Leads the "Green Bridge of Generations" program, bringing children and seniors together through gardening, herbs, harvesting, natural health traditions, and seasonal crafts. Her workshops help children explore seeds, soil, plants, and food through sensory, hands-on activities while building relationships across generations and preserving local gardening and herbal traditions.

anna.name: Anna Dulny-Szczodrak
anna.description: Led hands-on workshops helping students learn about seeds, soil, composting, plant care, and school garden stewardship, with a special focus on using CAD design.

tomasz.name: Tomasz Kot
tomasz.description: Helped students create a biodiverse school garden with raised beds, herbs, vegetables, strawberries, a flower meadow, an insect-friendly bed, and a fruit tree. His workshops introduced students to plant growth, permaculture-inspired gardening, pollinators, healthy eating, and the importance of green spaces in cities.

dagmara.name: Dagmara Wawrzyńczyk
dagmara.description: Led students in designing and creating a school garden that raised awareness about climate change, composting, biodiversity, pollinators, healthy eating, and growing food without artificial fertilizers. The project included site inventory and design work, planting vegetables, fruits, flowers, and ornamental plants, and creating a green space for learning, recreation, and community use.

rybnik.title: Rybnik: A Model City for School Gardens and Social Cohesion
rybnik.description: In partnership with the City of Rybnik, Resiliency Gardens helped establish a model city program that has supported 23 school gardens across the city and demonstrated how public schools, local government, NGOs, businesses, and community leaders can work together to connect children with nature, food, and environmental stewardship. Building on the success of the Resiliency Gardens model, Rybnik began funding an additional six schools on its own in 2026 through its “Towards a Green Future” initiative, further expanding access to garden-based environmental education across the city.

localGovernment.title: 2024 Innovative Local Government Award
localGovernment.description: Recognition from the Polish Press Agency for Rybnik’s leadership in the Resiliency Gardens project.

krakow.title: Kraków: Incubating the Next Generation of School Garden Innovation
krakow.description: The Resiliency Gardens Incubator in Kraków is designed to help educators, community gardeners, and schools test and share practical approaches to garden-based environmental education. The project will develop a children’s educational demonstration garden, a School Garden Starter Kit, and teacher workshops that can help more schools integrate food, nature, and sustainability into learning.

cards.title: Sensory development
cards.text: A garden is a place of wonder for a child. Children are absorbed by the textures, shapes, colors and scents of living plants and thrilled when they can enjoy their taste.  Gardening helps kids develop hand-eye coordination and build physical strength and important motor skills, such as cutting, planting, and writing.

cards.title: Intellectual skills
cards.text: Gardening involves planning, a skill that everyone needs. Kids should be included in this process. Support them in learning how to prepare the soil, plant, water, and weed.  They can report on what they have done already and what they think they should do next. In time, they will be able to identify the differences and characteristics of roots, stems, flowers, leaves, seeds and fruits. Gardening is a fun way to help kids learn something useful!

cards.title: Social skills
cards.text: Kids learn to cooperate by working together to nurture and care for their plants. They can paint flowerpots together and share their knowledge of different plants. Through planting trees or plants at school, they can meet new friends, gain status and expand their knowledge.

partnersSection.title: Our Community of Support
partnersSection.subtext: Resiliency Gardens has grown because people and organizations believed that children deserve the chance to learn from nature, grow food, care for the planet, and build healthier, more resilient communities. Our supporters include individual donors, foundations, local businesses, city partners, and friends who have helped plant the seeds of this work from the very beginning.

cards.text: Seed Programs International provides good quality seed, expertise, and training materials to humanitarian organizations working around the world to alleviate hunger and poverty. SPI’s in-kind grants have helped 27 schools in Poland to establish Resiliency Gardens for learning and sharing.

Rybnik, in southern Poland, leads in sustainable food practices. Through the StratKIT+ project, Rybnik has matched 10% of Resiliency Gardens grants, improving school garden infrastructure. Since 2024, 4,562 students from eleven schools are participating in gardening, enhancing community engagement and integrating sustainable food systems into education.

KidsGardening.org creates opportunities for kids to play, learn, and grow through gardening. KG’s in-kind donation of Learning Tools for educators, parents and child caregivers are now available in Polish and Ukrainian.

cards.name: Rachel E. Golden Foundation
cards.text: The Rachel E. Golden Foundation supports small, original, and innovative changemakers working to build a more humane, healthy, and hopeful world. Rooted in Rachel Golden’s belief in the healing and connective power of nature, the Foundation invests in practical, creative, early-stage initiatives that strengthen communities, restore connection, and grow lasting sources of resilience and hope.

Grupa Robocza Foundation is a Kraków-based foundation dedicated to innovative design education and interdisciplinary collaboration. With a planet-centered approach to technology and experimentation, Grupa Robocza creates space for people from different fields to develop practical and imaginative solutions. By providing local matching support for the Resiliency Gardens Incubator in Kraków, the Foundation is helping educators and community partners grow new models for outdoor learning, environmental education, and resilient food systems.

friends.title: Friends of Resiliency Gardens
friends.firstText: Resiliency Gardens took root because individual donors believed in the idea before it was widely known. Many of our earliest supporters were family members, friends and people moved by the need to help children reconnect with nature, food, and one another during a time of upheaval. Their generosity helped launch our first school gardens, support local educators, welcome Ukrainian children into shared learning spaces, and grow a model that cities and communities can now adapt.
friends.secondText: Every gift has helped Resiliency Gardens take root and grow. We are deeply grateful to all of our donors, including those who remain anonymous, and honored to recognize the individuals and families below who have given permission to be named.

donateCta.title: Help plant the next seeds of resilience.
donateCta.text: Your support makes it possible for children and youth to learn from nature, take part in sustainable food systems, build confidence and well-being, and care for the health of our planet. Every gift helps grow gardens, support local educators, and create learning experiences that can shape young lives for years to come.
